instruction: Enable the screen magnifier zoom feature so I can magnify parts of my display.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: ZOOM_ENABLED=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-magnifier-enabled 2>/dev/null); if echo "$ZOOM_ENABLED" | grep -q 'true'; then echo "Screen magnifier zoom enabled"; else echo "Screen magnifier zoom not enabled"; fi

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened GNOME Settings via system menu, navigated to Accessibility section, and toggled Large Text ON in 7 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate GNOME Settings sidebar, find Accessibility section, toggle switches on/off
metadata.task_rationale: Tests enabling screen zoom from the same Accessibility panel - the original evaluator already checked zoom as an alternative success path, but the model chose Large Text. This variation specifically requires the zoom approach.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the screen magnifier via Settings > Accessibility > Zoom. Evaluator checks if screen-magnifier-enabled is set to true via gsettings.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses gsettings to check org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-magnifier-enabled, which is the correct GNOME setting for screen magnifier zoom
Shell command logic correctly distinguishes enabled vs not-enabled states with distinct output strings
